set.typical_award_size: Requirement and entitlement incentive, not a subsidy. Ordinance 1378 (adopted January 20, 2026) repealed the 2008 article (Ord. 1113) and re-enacted Article 36.5 (Sections 10.08.4650 to 10.08.4686). Density bonus tables in 10.08.4659 run from 20% (10% low income or 5% very low income) up to 50% (24% low or 15% very low); lower income student housing 35% to 50%; moderate income for-sale common interest developments 5% to 50%; senior housing or mobile home park a flat 20%. The 10.08.4653 definition still says no more than 35%, but the tables control. One to five concessions or incentives (10.08.4677), five for 100% lower income projects plus up to three stories or 33 feet near major transit; parking caps, land donation (15% base) and child care bonuses; recorded density bonus housing agreement (10.08.4686).
set.affordability_requirement: Bonus under 10.08.4659 for any one of: 10% low income, 5% very low income, a senior housing development or mobile home park, 20% lower income students in student housing, or 10% moderate income units in a for-sale common interest development. Section 10.08.4656 still lists older thresholds (10% very low, 20% low, 50% senior, 20% moderate condominium). Code defines low income eligibility at 70% AMI and very low at 50% AMI, with affordable rent set at 60% and 50% AMI; 100% lower income projects may include up to 20% moderate income units.
set.next_deadline: Applies at entitlement; no application deadline. Ordinance 1378 is in effect and no further hearing is scheduled.
set.audit_note: City spot check Nov 9, 2026: typical_award_size said the bonus runs 5% to 35%; the adopted 10.08.4659 tables run to 50% (24% low or 15% very low). affordability_requirement listed only the 10% very low and 20% low thresholds; 10.08.4659 grants a bonus at 10% low or 5% very low income, plus student and 10% moderate for-sale tiers. next_deadline reworded to remove the past adoption date as a deadline.
